Read against the row's two outcomes:

* **Every seed of the sample draws at 1 100 / 50 and at every larger frame** (1 200, 1 600, 2 000, CITY: 12 / 12 each),
  and the reroll moves S5's root at 12 / 12 where it was run there. Below it the count falls: 10, 9, 0. That is
  outcome (a)'s shape, and 1 100 / 50 is the first frame of the sweep at which every seed draws. CONFIRMED.
* **At M0-d-09's test frame** the growth stage proper draws at no seed; the only stream S5 reads there is
  `growth.mainroad` (S5b's, M0-c-04's), and the `{ S5: 1 }` moves are site seeds 4 and 9 and fusion seeds 6 and 9 —
  the queue row's figures for M0-c-04 S5's tree, which the base carries. CONFIRMED.
* **S5d draws at no seed of any frame.** It draws only when an unwalled stage's top-up grows a rim that holds a seed.
  On the stand-in demand (C-0254 (10); S2's real demand is the item's listed defer to M1) the top-up ran once in the
  228 runs — site 400 / 12, seed 11, stage 3 — and its rim held no seed. The builder's sentence "`topUp` `none` in all
  360 runs" is wrong at that seed (N-s3c-2); the claim that S5d draws nowhere stands. The item's own S5d tests
  (`capacity.test.ts`: a stage short by > 5 % takes one top-up and grows its rim) are green in NEAR, so the stage is
  built; the fixture's demand simply does not ask for it. Not a defect of S5d. CONFIRMED (the counts); PLAUSIBLE (the
  reading).
* **One seed draws without moving the root:** site 900 / 30 seed 4 holds one seed, makes one proposal (one curvature
  and one heading draw) and keeps no street at either reroll, so its S5 root is the same under `{ S5: 1 }`. That is why
  10 seeds move there, not 11. Informative.
